data.name: SharedAccountsNote
data.value: Shared accounts are counted once. Ownership is not split into percentages.

data.name: SecuritiesNote
data.value: Securities value only, excluding cash. The latest valuation on or before the balance date counts. No individual shares, live prices or crypto.

data.name: DeleteValuationQuestion
data.value: Delete this securities valuation? Cash and transactions remain unchanged.

data.name: DefaultBudgetNote
data.value: Default budgets apply monthly. A different monthly budget does not change other months. Budget 0 = no limit. Budgets apply to the whole household with an owner filter.

data.name: AnnualActualNote
data.value: Only entries through today. Future months are not plotted. After savings = income minus spending and set aside; not an account balance.

data.name: AnnualBudgetNote
data.value: Annual budgets cover 12 months, not just the period through today. Budgets apply to the household, even with an owner filter. Budget 0 = no limit.

data.name: PlannedTransactionsNote
data.value: Future entries count as actual only on their date. Categories determine ordinary income/spending, savings or movements between your own accounts. Categorizing never changes balances. Previously recorded transfers retain their original treatment.

data.name: DeleteManualTransferQuestion
data.value: Delete this manual transfer? Its balance effects disappear from both accounts.

data.name: DeleteTransactionQuestion
data.value: Delete this entry? Any transfer decision is removed; the other bank entry remains and counts again as ordinary income/spending.

data.name: BackupSecurityNote
data.value: A database backup contains all financial data. CSV includes all transactions regardless of filters and is not a complete restore copy. Potential spreadsheet formulas are neutralised. Databases and backups are not encrypted; store downloads securely. The website cannot open a Windows folder on the server.

data.name: DatabasePreservesNote
data.value: Import your existing Huishoudboek database or database backup (.db). Transactions, custom descriptions, accounts, owners, budgets, rules, recurring payments, valuations, mortgage and import history are preserved. Your source file is not changed.

data.name: HomeAssistantStorageNote
data.value: After importing, your records run entirely in persistent Home Assistant storage. No Windows computer with the financial app or shared network folder is needed.

data.name: DatabaseRestoreWarning
data.value: Prefer a backup from the app. Otherwise close both the Windows app and financial service before copying the database: copying only an active .db may miss recent changes. Import replaces all records for ALL users. File format, supported version, SQLite integrity and financial references are checked first; then a safety copy of the current records is made. The file is uploaded only after explicit confirmation. Maximum 64 MB.

data.name: RulesOrderNote
data.value: Rules run in the order added; the first matching rule wins. Existing categories are preserved. Savings and own-account categories can use rules too. Only legacy transfers and explicit splits are skipped. Recognition can also match recurring payments.

data.name: RestoreDatabaseQuestion
data.value: This database replaces all shared records. The source file remains unchanged. A safety copy of the current data is saved first. Unsaved changes and import previews become invalid. Continue?

data.name: UndoImportQuestion
data.value: Undo this entire import? Transactions from this import, including those edited later, are removed. Other transactions and settings remain.

data.name: DeleteRuleQuestion
data.value: Delete this rule? Existing category assignments are preserved.

data.name: ApplyRulesQuestion
data.value: Apply rules to all existing uncategorized, non-internal payments? Existing categories are preserved; recognised recurring payments may be matched.

data.name: DatabaseImported

data.value: Recurring payments follow your dates and frequency. One matched bank entry replaces one planned payment with the actual amount and bank date. Other payments retain your estimate; amounts are not adjusted automatically.

data.name: AssumptionOverdue
data.value: The latest overdue unmatched expense per recurring payment is reserved tomorrow. Older missing payments are not added up. Overdue income is not assumed received. Check matches and schedules.

data.value: Additional daily spending uses the average of up to {0} days through the last imported bank date (without an import: today). Matched recurring bills, mortgages and confirmed transfers are excluded. Planned variable payments fill the daily average rather than being added on top.

data.value: Spending headroom is the lowest balance through the next income day, minus your buffer, with a minimum of 0. The purchase check covers at least 30 days, or longer if income arrives later (up to {0} days). Costs conservatively precede income even on income day.

data.value: Shared accounts are counted once. No automatic movement of savings, investments or money from other accounts; only explicitly recorded future transfers count. Unexpected expenses, holidays, interest and changed amounts are excluded unless you plan them.

data.value: Give savings a category that counts as ‘Savings & investments’. Movements between current accounts count as ‘Between own accounts’. Use the same treatment on both sides if you import both accounts. No need to match two entries; categorizing never changes balances.

data.name: SavingsCountingNote
data.value: Net set aside = debits minus receipts in savings categories on current accounts, on their own bank date. The savings/investment side is not counted again. A withdrawal reduces contributions, not income. This is not a balance or investment return. The owner filter follows the current account.

data.name: OwnAccountCountingNote
data.value: These categories count as neither income, spending nor savings. Use this treatment on both sides of movements between your current accounts or between savings/investment accounts. Bank amounts still affect their own account balances.

data.name: CategoryHistoryNote
data.value: Changing ‘Counts as’ or deleting a category also changes historical reports, never bank amounts or balances.
